bullets.text: Q2 CR was 85.4; YTD CR 84.3 was substantially better than estimates of the dramatically improving industry average (94.2 reported for Q1); results benefited from continuing low frequency of reported claims.

Claim frequency lower than comparable 2003 quarterly and annual periods on all coverages; personal auto bodily injury severity trend annualized at 2–5%; physical damage severity trend was closer to flat.
Q2 NPW grew 11%, demonstrating solid but slowing expansion; management aims to maintain momentum by continuing to pursue new business growth into the second half of 2004 whenever smart.

Insurance cycle shifting from 'hard' to 'soft'; very low rate inflation and stable or lower renewal rates led to fewer consumers shopping, alongside heightened marketing intensity from profitable competitors.

Fewer consumers are shopping amid stable renewal pricing, and new business growth is expected to slow; second-half objectives emphasize maintaining momentum, increasing policy retention, and seeking new business growth when smart.

Concierge physical damage claims service completed a very good first half, consistently meeting key expansion specifications; Progressive is looking to establish four more Florida service centers and scouting locations in four other states.

Customer service group restructured into three aligned groups: agency customers, direct customers, and independent agents and brokers; initiatives aim to deliver targeted improvements, efficiencies, and an independent agency brand communication strategy.

Progressive is now the #1 auto insurance writer in Rhode Island and Vermont; the company is in discussions with New Jersey regarding the regulatory environment required for Progressive to consider doing business there.
Best service at lowest price is seen as winning formula across hard and soft market cycles; company remains focused on ultimate goal of becoming Consumers’ #1 Choice for Auto Insurance.

Claims staffing and training are in control; the expected slower hiring period will be used to solidify gains and expand training in preparation for faster growth that management believes will occur in the future.
